title: Raktabija and the Mothers
hookLine: the gods' powers step out as goddesses, and Kali catches every drop of the demon Blood-Seed
carry: shakti: every god's power is a goddess
tomorrow: Shumbha says she fights with borrowed strength. what does she answer?

cards: Every drop: the eighth chapter's problem. His generals dead, Shumbha sends out his whole army, and something new happens. From the bodies of the gods, their powers step out, each a goddess in that god's own form.
From Brahma, one on a swan, with prayer beads and a water pot. From Shiva, one on a bull, holding a trident. From Vishnu, one on Garuda, the great bird.
From Indra, one on an elephant, with a thunderbolt. A boar-faced goddess. A lion-faced goddess.
They gather around the goddess. Then a demon walks out to meet them: Raktabija. Blood-Seed.

teach.b: First the goddess does something surprising. From her own body comes one more power, fierce, howling like a pack of jackals, and she gives Shiva himself a job: go to Shumbha and Nishumbha as my messenger.
Give heaven back and go home to the underworld, or come and fight. Because Shiva was her messenger, she's called Shivaduti. The demons choose to fight.
His power is in his name: whenever a drop of his blood falls to the ground, a new demon rises from it, just as strong.
The goddesses strike him with thunderbolt, spear, discus, trident, and each wound makes it worse. Soon the field is full of him, and the gods are terrified. So the goddess, smiling, turns to Kali.
In paraphrase: open your mouth wide, and take in every drop before it touches the ground. Kali does. As the goddess strikes, Kali drinks the blood and swallows the new demons as they rise.
The drops stop landing. Drained, Raktabija falls. Notice what wins.
Not a bigger weapon; every weapon only made more of him. What wins is catching the thing before it can grow again. And notice who won it: goddesses.
Even the power of Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu stepped out of them as a woman.

teach.h: SHAKTI: EVERY GOD'S POWER IS A GODDESS.
teach.b: That's the teaching called shakti: in Shakta Hinduism, a god's power is the goddess herself. Temples still carve the Mothers in a row. Some readers also hear in Raktabija a craving that multiplies each time it's fed.

how: The goddesses who come out of the gods in the eighth chapter are known together as the Matrikas, the Mothers, and groups of them are carved and worshiped in some Hindu temples.

a roll call of the gods' powers as goddesses
a spell that stops blood from touching the ground

games.q: the eighth chapter — tap the pairs.
p: every drop of blood becomes a demon
she sends Shiva as her messenger
catches every drop before it lands

s: the goddesses beat Raktabija with stronger weapons
every wound made more of him. Kali catching the blood before it landed is what turned the fight.
the goddess sends Shiva as her messenger
so she is called Shivaduti, the one whose messenger is Shiva.
the goddesses who step out of the gods are each god's own power
Brahma's on a swan, Shiva's on a bull, Vishnu's on Garuda, Indra's with a thunderbolt: in Shakta teaching, a god's power, his shakti, is a goddess.

games.q: you're the goddess. every time you wound Raktabija, his blood hits the ground and becomes another demon. the field is filling up. what do you do?
o: tell Kali to open her mouth and catch every drop.
retreat and wait for the gods.
games.why: smiling, she tells Kali to open her mouth wide. Kali drinks the blood before it lands, and Raktabija, drained, falls.

practice: Let a small irritation come to mind and watch one thought grow from it, then another: that's the multiplying.
Gently go back to the first one, without feeding or fighting it, and let it settle on the breath out before it can land; if it multiplies again, come back again.
If you pray, ask for help in your own words; if you don't, let the breath be what catches it.

wordCard.voice: The Devi Mahatmya. Today, the gods' powers as goddesses, the Mothers, and Raktabija, beaten when Kali caught every drop.

orig.note: Sanskrit: rakta-bīja, blood-seed. The demon whose every drop of blood becomes another of him.

carryVoice: Your line: shakti, every god's power is a goddess. Every weapon made more of Raktabija; Kali's open mouth caught the drops. A new week, well begun.

sources.ref: Devi Mahatmya, chapter 8 (the Matrikas; Shivaduti; Raktabija)
